items.q: Lan: Where's Nam? / Mai: He ______ dumplings in the kitchen since noon.
items.vi: Lan: Nam đâu rồi? / Mai: Cậu ấy gói bánh trong bếp từ trưa tới giờ.
items.explanation: Since noon marks an action that started in the past and is still going on, so the present perfect continuous has been making is needed.

items.q: I still ______ Nam fifty thousand dong for the bánh mì he bought me yesterday.
items.vi: Tôi vẫn còn nợ Nam năm mươi nghìn tiền ổ bánh mì cậu ấy mua cho tôi hôm qua.
items.explanation: Owe someone money = you must pay it back. Own means possess, lend is giving money out, and keep does not take two objects like this.

items.q: Lan: Sorry, I'm an hour late for the dumpling class! / Nam: Well, ______.
items.vi: Lan: Xin lỗi, mình đến lớp gói bánh trễ cả tiếng! / Nam: Thôi, trễ còn hơn không.
items.explanation: Better late than never is what you say when someone arrives late but you are still glad they came. The other three are real sayings, but they do not answer an apology for being late.

items.q: Lan ______ a photo of the lantern display and sent it to her cousin in Da Nang.
items.vi: Lan chụp một tấm ảnh gian trưng bày lồng đèn rồi gửi cho em họ ở Đà Nẵng.
items.explanation: English says take a photo (here in the past: took). Make, do and get do not collocate with a photo in this sense.

items.q: Everyone in our street ______ to buy lanterns for the Mid-Autumn party.
items.vi: Cả xóm tôi góp tiền mua lồng đèn cho buổi tiệc Trung thu.
items.explanation: Chip in = each person gives some money towards a shared cost. Drop in is a short visit, chip away is to remove bit by bit, and give in is to surrender.

items.q: Lan: The bánh chưng is burnt! / Nam: You ______ the heat on so high.
items.vi: Lan: Bánh chưng bị khét rồi! / Nam: Đáng lẽ cậu không nên để lửa to như thế.
items.explanation: Shouldn't have + past participle criticises a past action that was a mistake. Needn't have means it was unnecessary, couldn't have is a deduction (it was impossible), and mustn't have is not a form English uses for past criticism.

items.q: We can't ______ to eat out every night, so I cook at home most days.
items.vi: Nhà tôi không đủ tiền ăn ngoài mỗi tối, nên hầu như ngày nào tôi cũng nấu ở nhà.
items.explanation: Can't afford to do something = not have enough money for it. Pay and spend need an amount or object, and cost takes a thing, not a person, as its subject.

items.q: The town ______ my grandparents live is famous for its floating market.
items.vi: Thị trấn nơi ông bà tôi sống nổi tiếng với chợ nổi.
items.explanation: My grandparents live is a complete clause, so the relative adverb where (= in which) is needed after a place. Which and that would need a preposition (in which), and who is for people.

items.q: This time next week we ______ mooncakes at the Mid-Autumn fair.
items.vi: Giờ này tuần sau chúng ta sẽ đang ăn bánh trung thu ở hội chợ Trung thu.
items.explanation: This time next week points to an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous will be eating is correct.

items.q: If we don't hurry, we'll ______ the last bus home.
items.vi: Nếu không nhanh lên, chúng ta sẽ lỡ chuyến xe buýt cuối về nhà.
items.explanation: You miss a bus, a train or a plane when you arrive too late for it. Lose, drop and fail do not collocate with the bus.

items.q: My mother is very proud ______ her recipe for fish sauce dressing.
items.vi: Mẹ tôi rất tự hào về công thức nước mắm chấm của bà.
items.explanation: The adjective proud is always followed by of: proud of someone / something.

items.q: Remember to ______ the cookery book to the library by Friday.
items.vi: Nhớ trả cuốn sách nấu ăn cho thư viện trước thứ Sáu nhé.
items.explanation: Return = give something back. Borrow is taking it, lend is giving your own thing out, and you rent a room or a bike, not a library book.

items.q: Half the class ______ flu after eating ice cream in the rain at the fair.
items.vi: Nửa lớp bị cúm sau khi ăn kem dưới mưa ở hội chợ.
items.explanation: Come down with an illness = start to suffer from it. Come up with is to think of an idea, put up with is to tolerate, and come across is to find by chance.

items.q: Wrapping bánh chưng takes ______ patience, so my grandmother starts early in the morning.
items.vi: Gói bánh chưng cần rất nhiều kiên nhẫn, nên bà tôi bắt đầu từ sáng sớm.
items.explanation: Patience is uncountable, so it takes a great deal of (= a lot of). A large number of, a few and many go only with plural countable nouns.

items.q: Nam keeps promising to help clean up after the festival, but ______.
options: every cloud has a silver lining
two heads are better than one
items.vi: Nam cứ hứa sẽ giúp dọn dẹp sau lễ hội, nhưng hành động mới nói lên tất cả.
items.explanation: Actions speak louder than words = what you do matters more than what you promise. The other sayings are about practice, bad luck and teamwork, so they do not fit.

items.q: We're all looking forward ______ the lantern parade next week.
items.vi: Tất cả chúng tôi đều mong được xem lễ rước đèn tuần tới.
items.explanation: In look forward to, to is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund: to seeing, not the infinitive.

items.q: The restaurant will ______ your phở to your door within thirty minutes.
items.vi: Nhà hàng sẽ giao phở tới tận cửa nhà bạn trong vòng ba mươi phút.
items.explanation: Deliver = take goods to someone's home. You order or receive food as a customer, and a restaurant serves food at the table, not to your door.

items.q: You won't find a seat at the night market food stalls ______ you get there before six.
items.vi: Bạn sẽ không kiếm được chỗ ngồi ở các quầy ăn chợ đêm trừ khi bạn tới đó trước sáu giờ.
items.explanation: Unless = if ... not: you will not find a seat if you do not arrive before six. If would give the opposite meaning, although shows contrast, and so that shows purpose.

items.q: Nam: Why weren't you at the parade? / Lan: Something ______ at home just as I was leaving.
items.vi: Nam: Sao cậu không đến xem diễu hành? / Lan: Có chuyện phát sinh ở nhà đúng lúc mình chuẩn bị đi.
items.explanation: Just as I was leaving fixes the event at a finished moment in the past, so the past simple cropped up (= happened unexpectedly) is correct, not a present form.

items.q: I wish I ______ how to make mooncakes as well as my grandmother does.
items.vi: Ước gì tôi biết làm bánh trung thu ngon như bà tôi.
items.explanation: A wish about a present situation uses wish + past simple: I wish I knew. Had known would be a regret about the past, and know / would know are not used after wish here.

items.q: Could you ______ the table while I fry the fish?
items.vi: Con dọn bàn ăn giúp mẹ trong lúc mẹ chiên cá nhé?
items.explanation: You lay (or set) the table = put plates and cutlery on it before a meal. Put, place and fix do not form this collocation.

items.q: Red envelopes ______ to children on the first morning of Tet.
items.vi: Bao lì xì được trao cho trẻ em vào sáng mùng Một Tết.
items.explanation: The envelopes receive the action, so the present simple passive are given is needed: be + past participle.

items.q: Can you ______ me a few minutes to explain the new bus route?
items.vi: Bạn có thể dành cho mình vài phút để giải thích tuyến xe buýt mới không?
items.explanation: Spare someone a few minutes = give them a little of your time. Share, save and spend do not take this pattern with a person and time.

items.q: Mai said she ______ the flower market the next morning to buy peach blossom.
items.vi: Mai nói sáng hôm sau cô ấy sẽ đi chợ hoa mua cành đào.
items.explanation: In reported speech after said, will becomes would: would visit. The other forms do not shift the tense back.

items.q: The traffic in the city centre is ______ than it was five years ago.
items.vi: Giao thông ở trung tâm thành phố tệ hơn nhiều so với năm năm trước.
items.explanation: Than needs a comparative: worse, and it can be strengthened with far or much. More worse is a double comparative, and worst is a superlative.
